title: The three load procedures look scheduled twice
detail: dwh_nightly.py runs all three procedures after landing SAP files, while SQL Agent DWH_Nightly runs sp_Load_ProductionRun and sp_Build_Invoice as their own steps and DWH_Inventory runs the snapshot at 23:55.
impact: The target job graph cannot be drawn until it is known which caller is real

evidence.excerpt: PROCS = ["EXEC mfg.sp_Load_ProductionRun", "EXEC sales.sp_Build_Invoice @OrderDateKey = ?",
DWH_Nightly,2 mfg.sp_Load_ProductionRun ... DWH_Inventory,1 supply.sp_Snapshot_Inventory

meaning: Two schedulers appear to run the same loads; one may be dead code, or both really run
risk: If both run, the snapshot is rebuilt at 01:00 for an order date with that night's stock, and time is wasted in a full window

recommendation.reason: Both callers are stated; whether both fire needs the Agent job export (OQ-05)

title: Twelve datetimeoffset columns span three plant time zones
detail: StartedAt, OccurredAt, ReportedAt, ReceivedAt, ApprovedAt, IssuedAt, OrderedAt (3 tables), CreatedAt, ShippedAt, DeliveredAt keep a UTC offset. The production day is CAST(started_at AS DATE) in the MES offset.
impact: Delta timestamps keep the instant, not the offset; the plant-local day must be stored explicitly

evidence.excerpt: `datetimeoffset` in three plant time zones; the Power BI model converts to UTC and nobody remembers exactly where
WHERE CAST(r.started_at AS DATE) = @LoadDate;

meaning: Times recorded in local plant time could shift day when moved, changing daily OEE and order dates
risk: Night-shift runs and late orders land on another day, so daily reconciliation fails

recommendation.reason: Column types read from DDL; DBA and kickoff name the risk

title: Duplicate product 7 may double production runs
detail: mfg.PackagingProduct has ProductKey 7 twice and no key. The production load joins it on Sku; if both rows share a SKU, every MES run of that SKU is inserted twice.
impact: UnitsProduced, an acceptance sum, may already be overstated in the source

evidence.excerpt: JOIN mfg.PackagingProduct AS p ON p.Sku = r.sku
No primary key: the load of 2021-03 inserted ProductKey 7 twice

meaning: The known duplicate product row could be inflating production figures, not just the product list
risk: Fixing DWH-412 on the target then makes UnitsProduced lower than the source and reconciliation fails

recommendation.reason: Inferred from the join; a count of SKUs for key 7 on the test copy settles it (OQ-11)

title: Inner joins drop unmatched runs and stock silently
detail: Production runs with an unknown machine or SKU, and stock lines with an unknown warehouse code, are left out by INNER JOIN; nothing is logged or counted.
impact: The target needs a quarantine or reject count so losses become visible

evidence.excerpt: JOIN mfg.Machine AS m ON m.ExternalId = r.machine_ext_id
JOIN supply.Warehouse AS w ON w.WarehouseCode = s.warehouse_code

meaning: Some production and stock may never reach the reports, and nobody knows how much
risk: Copied as-is, the loss continues unmeasured; changed, the target stops matching the source

recommendation.reason: Read verbatim in two procedures

title: Several loaders and objects are missing from the folder
detail: Not supplied: sequences seq_Invoice and seq_Snapshot, SSIS packages the config mentions, SQL Agent job definitions, loaders of MachineEvent, EnergyReading, master data and LIMS, the wms.stock_extract producer, the sustainability extract, report definitions.
impact: Scope and effort cannot be closed until these are exported

evidence.excerpt: ; Connection strings of the packaging DWH tooling (SSIS configurations, the Python loaders in jobs/).
DWH_Nightly,3 LIMS hourly catch-up,2026-09-29 01:55,95,succeeded

meaning: Part of what feeds the warehouse has not been handed over yet
risk: Wave plans built without them miss feeds, and hot tables go stale on the target

recommendation.reason: Names in code, config and job history with no matching file

title: The reject check fires after the rows are written
detail: sp_Load_ProductionRun deletes and inserts the day, then THROWs if rejects exceed production, with no transaction. Since UnitsProduced = good + rejected, the check can only fire on negative good units.
impact: Rebuild as an expectation that rolls back the day, checked on the MES values

evidence.excerpt: IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mfg.ProductionRun WHERE ProductionDateKey = @DateKey AND UnitsRejected > UnitsProduced)
r.units_good + r.units_rejected

meaning: The quality gate on production data is weaker than the spec suggests
risk: A faithful port keeps a gate that almost never fires and leaves bad rows behind when it does

recommendation.reason: Read verbatim; the commit behaviour under SQL Agent is standard T-SQL

title: The inventory snapshot takes 40 minutes and timed out at month end
detail: sp_Snapshot_Inventory ran 2,390 s on 2026-09-28 and failed on timeout after 4,110 s on 2026-08-31 (DWH-401). It recomputes 28 days of order-line demand per stock row.
impact: Re-architect: compute demand once per product and day, not per row; do not transpile as-is

evidence.excerpt: DWH_Inventory,1 supply.sp_Snapshot_Inventory,2026-08-31 23:55,4110,failed: timeout (DWH-401)

meaning: The slowest step of the night, and it fails exactly when month-end stock values matter
risk: Ported unchanged, it costs the same time on compute billed by the second

recommendation.reason: Measured in job history; matches the ticket

title: Invoice values depend on the day the build runs
detail: IssuedAt and DueDate use SYSDATETIME(), and a rebuild overwrites amounts on existing invoices; vw_OpenReceivables also computes against today.
impact: Reconciliation must pin a cut-off moment and compare both sides at that moment

evidence.excerpt: WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET NetAmount = src.NetAmount, TaxAmount = src.TaxAmount,
DATEDIFF(day, i.DueDate, CAST(SYSDATETIME() AS DATE)) AS DaysOverdue,

meaning: Receivables numbers move with the clock, so two runs a day apart never match to the cent
risk: Reconciliation shows false differences and delays sign-off

recommendation.reason: Read verbatim

title: Invoices of customers without payment terms are never chased
detail: DueDate = DATEADD(day, PaymentTermsDays, ...) is NULL when PaymentTermsDays is NULL (the column allows it); vw_OpenReceivables requires DueDate < today, so such invoices never appear.
impact: Profile NULL terms on the test copy; decide a default on the target

evidence.excerpt: DATEADD(day, (SELECT c.PaymentTermsDays FROM sales.Customer c WHERE c.CustomerKey = src.CustomerKey), SYSDATETIME())
[PaymentTermsDays] TINYINT NULL,

meaning: Some unpaid invoices may be invisible to Finance's dunning list
risk: Receivables understated on both platforms; magnitude unknown until profiled

recommendation.reason: Follows from two verbatim lines; magnitude not measured

title: Invoice amounts are in order currency with a fixed rate of 1
detail: Net, tax and gross stay in the order's currency and ExchangeRate is written as 1.0. The acceptance criterion sums NetAmount and GrossAmount without naming a currency.
impact: Acceptance sums must be per currency, or a conversion source must be found

evidence.excerpt: src.Currency, src.NetAmount, src.TaxAmount, src.NetAmount + src.TaxAmount, 1.0, 0, SYSDATETIME());
the sums of `UnitsProduced`, `NetAmount`, `GrossAmount`, `StockValueEur` match the source

meaning: Totals across currencies mix euro, krona and others into one number
risk: A total that matches proves nothing; one that differs cannot be explained

recommendation.reason: Hard-coded value read verbatim

title: Sequences and IDENTITY keys need a value-preserving design
detail: Invoice and snapshot keys come from sequences; Customer and Supplier use IDENTITY, which SAP loads depend on. Delta identity columns do not guarantee consecutive values and do not continue an existing series.
impact: Design key generation for waves 1–2: load existing keys, then a controlled generator

evidence.excerpt: use IDENTITY; the SAP loads depend on the generated values being stable
NEXT VALUE FOR sales.seq_Invoice

meaning: Customer, supplier and invoice numbers must stay the same after the move
risk: New keys break SAP loads and customer-visible invoice numbers

recommendation.reason: DBA states the dependency; code shows the sequences

title: Business logic lives in Power BI models that are out of scope
detail: The Power BI model converts times to UTC (location unknown) and de-duplicates product 7, while the model rewrite is excluded from this project.
impact: Capture model logic before cut-over even though the rewrite is elsewhere

evidence.excerpt: Out of scope: Power BI model rewrite (separate project), SSRS retirement.
Power BI de-duplicates in the model

meaning: Two fixes the business relies on sit in reports nobody in this project will touch
risk: Repointed models double-correct or stop correcting once the target fixes DWH-412

recommendation.reason: Kickoff, spec and interview all state it

title: IDENTITY keys: the DBA names five tables, the DDL shows two
detail: The DBA lists Customer, Supplier, Inspection, MaintenanceWorkOrder and Shipment as IDENTITY. The DDL export shows IDENTITY only on Customer and Supplier.
impact: Key design and SAP dependencies for three more tables are uncertain

evidence.excerpt: `sales.Customer`, `supply.Supplier`, `quality.Inspection`, `mfg.MaintenanceWorkOrder` and `supply.Shipment` use IDENTITY
[ShipmentKey] BIGINT NOT NULL,

meaning: Either the export lost the IDENTITY clauses or the DBA's list is out of date
risk: Keys planned as plain columns when SAP expects generated ones, or the reverse

recommendation.reason: Two sources disagree; a sys.identity_columns query settles it (OQ-07)

title: The DDL export is not a faithful script
detail: Customer and Supplier repeat IDENTITY(1, 1) twice, Shipment's primary key is written as one bracketed name, and headers carry Synapse terms (HASH, ROUND_ROBIN) that SQL Server does not use.
impact: Re-export with SSMS or mssql-scripter before running Lakebridge Analyzer on it

evidence.excerpt: [CustomerKey] INT IDENTITY(1, 1) IDENTITY(1, 1) NOT NULL,
CONSTRAINT [PK_Shipment] PRIMARY KEY NONCLUSTERED ([ShipmentKey, ShipDateKey])

meaning: The table scripts were edited after export and would not run as they stand
risk: An analyzer or transpiler fed this export reports errors or wrong keys

recommendation.reason: Invalid T-SQL read verbatim

title: Row counts come from a demo-sized copy, not production
detail: Every large table shows exactly 10,000 rows and a few MB, while the DBA describes a 2 TB data file. The export describes the test copy, not production volume.
impact: No volume, backfill or compute sizing can be concluded yet

evidence.excerpt: SQL Server 2019 Enterprise on `PACKDWH01`, 2 TB data file, 16 cores

meaning: The volume figures in hand cannot size the migration
risk: Estimates and backfill plans built on them are wrong by orders of magnitude

recommendation.reason: The cap at 10,000 and the 2 TB statement are both verbatim

title: No 90-day usage or runtime history yet
detail: sysjobhistory_90d.csv holds one run per step plus one failure, not 90 days. last_user_read comes from index-usage counters with no window start or restart date.
impact: No table, report or job may be called orphan; runtimes are single samples

schema_name,table_name,row_count,reserved_mb,last_user_read,last_user_write

meaning: The evidence to decide what to retire does not exist yet
risk: Retiring on this basis drops month-end or year-end objects

title: The test copy is reached over a public tunnel without certificate checks
detail: The [dwh] section points at bore.pub,60747, a public TCP tunnel host, with trust_server_certificate = yes, so the server certificate is not validated.
impact: Agree a private path (VPN, private link) before Lakehouse Federation reads it

trust_server_certificate = yes

risk: Interception or impersonation of the database; a client audit finding

recommendation.reason: Both settings read verbatim

title: The nightly job and the migration share one connection config
detail: dwh_nightly.py reads [dwh] from config/connections.ini, which now names the test copy and its read-only login. The production job would write through it.
impact: Separate configs per environment before any migration tooling is wired in

The test copy used for the Databricks migration is reachable at the host below

risk: The nightly load fails, or writes to the wrong database

title: SQL login with a password file and a shared service account
detail: The loader signs in with a SQL login whose password is read from a plain file on ETL02, and runs under the shared account svc_dwh_etl.
impact: The target uses a service principal and a secret scope; the file is retired

risk: Anyone with access to ETL02 can sign in to the warehouse

title: SAP files land straight into warehouse tables
detail: bcp appends every file matching the pattern on the share into sales and supply tables, with no staging, truncate or archive step. Files left on the share would be loaded again and fail on the primary keys.
impact: The target ingestion needs file tracking (e.g. Auto Loader) and a staging layer

meaning: Re-runs and leftover files are not handled by the load itself
risk: A re-run after a partial failure stops the nightly load or duplicates rows

recommendation.reason: Behaviour read in code; who moves the files is unknown (OQ-16)

title: Case-insensitive text becomes case-sensitive by default
detail: All text compares ignoring case except Inspection.BatchCode. Databricks compares strings case-sensitively unless a collation is set, which changes joins on codes and the email uniqueness rule.
impact: Choose a collation policy per column before conversion

evidence.excerpt: Every text column is `SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS` except `quality.Inspection.BatchCode`

meaning: Matches that work today because case is ignored may stop matching after the move
risk: Joins drop rows and duplicates slip through without any error

recommendation.reason: DBA states the collation; DDL shows the single exception

title: Personal data in customer, supplier and staff columns
detail: Customer and supplier contact emails, a customer phone, and staff identifiers or names in 14 tables. No erasure process is described.
impact: Define masking and grants in Unity Catalog before wave 1 lands

evidence.excerpt: [ContactEmail] NVARCHAR(120) NULL, [ContactPhone] VARCHAR(20) NULL,
[OperatorId] NVARCHAR(12) NULL,

meaning: The warehouse holds data about people, which needs access rules and an erasure path
risk: Copied with open grants, personal data becomes readable to every analyst

recommendation.reason: Columns read from DDL; erasure obligations need the DPO

title: Old OEE rows and money types limit 'to the cent' matching
detail: Oee before 2024-11 holds the MES value (DWH-388), and OEE factors are FLOAT. Money columns are MONEY with four decimals. Recomputed or retyped values will not match exactly.
impact: Compare stored values, not recomputed ones, and fix decimal types per column

evidence.excerpt: `mfg.ProductionRun.Oee` was stored as the MES value before 2024-11; rows older than that can differ
`MONEY` columns in `quality.Complaint` and `sales.*` round to four decimals

meaning: Some historic figures cannot be reproduced exactly from their inputs
risk: Reconciliation flags historic OEE as wrong and blocks sign-off

recommendation.reason: Spec and DBA state both facts

title: Comments and config disagree with the code
detail: The snapshot header says it scans supply.InventorySnapshot; the code scans sales.OrderLine. The MES config names database MES_PROD; the procedure reads catalog mes.

database = MES_PROD

risk: Low; wrong MES database would point ingestion at a replica

title: Two dunning levels exist side by side
detail: sales.Invoice stores a DunningLevel column, while vw_OpenReceivables computes ExpectedDunningLevel from days overdue. Nothing in the folder writes the stored column.
impact: Pick one as official for the target

meaning: Finance may see a different dunning level depending on where they look
risk: Low for the migration; confusing if both are carried

Move the four hot fact tables first and prove the OEE and receivables numbers match to the cent
